summary.text: A 1-year-old female Dalmatian presented with a 6-cm subcutaneous nodule near the right ischial tuberosity, with irregular borders, overlying erythema and mild mobility. The nodule was not painful on palpation, was not discomforting and did not interfere with walking, defecating or lying down. The differential diagnoses included a perianal hernia, anal sac fistula or abscess, and hygroma.

Fine needle aspiration cytology was performed to determine whether the nodule was inflammatory or neoplastic, using a 5-ml syringe and a 21-gauge needle. Serosanguineous, viscous fluid (5 ml) was aspirated, smeared, air-dried, stained with a rapid hemocolorant and evaluated by a veterinary clinical pathologist. Microscopy showed spindle cells, round cells consistent with histiocytes and a mucoid matrix with macrophages, and cytological findings did not indicate neoplastic, inflammatory or degenerative changes. A presumptive diagnosis of a ganglion cyst was made.

Histopathological confirmation was not possible and the owner decided against surgery. The lesion remained clinically stable during a follow-up period of 8 weeks, the last time the patient was seen, and the authors firmly believe the lesion is benign.

article_limitations: Figure captions are annotated without pixels in the annotation layer; actual images were inspected separately in visual.json.
Histopathological confirmation was not possible; the ganglion cyst diagnosis is presumptive and the benign nature is an author belief.
Synovial cyst is discussed only as a differentiating comparison and is not recorded as a differential diagnosis of this patient; whether imaging was performed is not stated for this patient.
Generic statements about cytology, ganglion cysts and resource-limited settings are background, not patient facts.
The caption places the nodule on the right ischial tuberosity while the text says near it; the text wording is used for body_site.

The Discussion sentence on fluid density, mucoid matrix and macrophages is read as this case's cytological evaluation ("revealed"); the spindle-cell cytoplasm is described as clear, irregular in the Case Description and elongated in the Discussion, kept as separate compatible items.
